problemStatement.plain:
For $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ let $f_r(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=a_1+\cdots+a_r$ with $a_i\in A$.

Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all large $n$) such that
$$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$
for all $x$?

$$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$
for all $x$?
